page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 vCPUs mapped across 6 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, running an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 24.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI are available alongside AES and FMA extensions. The instance includes 35 MB of shared L3 cache and a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. No local storage or discrete graphics accelerators are bundled with this instance type, requiring external network block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded and parallelized compute performance. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (1107.29) and Geekbench single-core (1018.0), register in the lower 25th percentile, reflecting the conservative 2.5 GHz base frequency and older Skylake-generation architecture. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks scale evenly across the 12 execution threads, producing average-tier outputs across stress-ng multi-core (8856.27), PassMark CPU (10201.54), and Geekbench multi-core (5135.0). Memory operations present balanced throughput for cached working sets at 493.85 GB/s, though uncached large-block read operations drop to 58.83 GB/s, reflecting an overall PassMark memory score in the bottom 25th percentile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.3xlarge provides dedicated CPU resource allocation without the pricing premium of memory-dense or GPU-enabled hardware profiles. The instance functions well for parallel workloads where memory consumption is strictly bounded by the 2.0 GB per core envelope, such as static web serving (yielding 8.31 GB/s throughput) and mid-volume in-memory caching (processing 8.65 million Redis SET operations per second). However, workloads demanding high single-thread clock rates, large local disk IOPS, or sizable LLM generation speeds show significant bottlenecks on this architecture.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance delivering 12 dedicated vCPUs and 24.0 GB of system memory on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 instruction support, and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote block storage volumes. Benchmark metrics reflect modest single-thread execution speeds alongside stable mid-tier multi-core compute throughput, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 10201.54 and Geekbench multi-core score of 5135.0. Memory bandwidth remains constrained on large-block operations, making this configuration best suited for horizontal web serving, clustered microservices, intermediate batch data processing, and caching layers with moderate memory footprints.
